Alan Chan et al., Visibility into AI Agents (FAccT 2024)

Chan and eleven co-authors argue that governing AI agents requires visibility: information about where, why, how, and by whom agents are used. They assess three measures — agent identifiers, real-time monitoring, and activity logs — and lay out implementations varying in intrusiveness and informativeness, including how to extend each to decentralised deployments through compute providers and tool providers. They then weigh their own proposals against privacy and concentration of power, concluding that visibility is necessary but not sufficient. A twelve-minute detailed summary followed by a three-minute critical Oggy Assessment.
